run.rulesInOwnWords:
Six tiers, position 1 (next to the LLM) to 6 (furthest out). Budgets 10,8,12,6,9,7; HOT marks 7,6,9,5,7,5; COLD marks 3,2,4,2,3,2; start holdings 3,6,6,2,2,1 (total 20); all tiers start COLD; stack ceiling 38. Each cycle runs five passes in order, and each pass covers all six tiers before the next pass starts.
1) Load: add the cycle's new chunks to each tier. Nothing is trimmed at this step.
2) Evict: go from tier 1 to tier 6 in order. If a tier is over budget, cut it to budget and add the excess to the next tier out. That tier is checked after it has received the excess. Excess from tier 6 is dropped and counted.
3) Flag: a COLD tier whose count is at or above its HOT mark becomes HOT. A HOT tier whose count is at or below its COLD mark becomes COLD. Any other tier keeps its flag. Each flip is logged.
4) Rebalance: work out all six amounts from the post-flag counts before moving anything. A COLD tier loses floor(count/4), which is dropped. A HOT tier gives floor(count/2) to the tier one step closer to the LLM; for tier 1 that amount is dropped. A tier can end this step over budget. That is left for the next cycle's evict, and after cycle 5 it simply stands.
5) Reset: if the stack total is above 38, every tier becomes floor(count/2) and the removed chunks are dropped. A total of exactly 38 does not trigger a reset.
One running drop count covers tier-6 eviction overflow, compactions, tier-1 promotions and reset removals.

gapsFlagged.rule: Flag pass, tier exactly at a mark
gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: I read 'at or above HOT' and 'at or below COLD' as inclusive and checked each against the tier's current flag only. HOT marks are always above COLD marks, so no tier can meet both conditions.

gapsFlagged.rule: Rebalance when a tier both gives and receives
gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: Each tier's amount comes from its own post-flag count before any transfers. Chunks it receives from the tier further out are added afterwards and are not compacted or passed on in the same cycle.
Each tier keeps floor(count/2), and the dropped amount is count minus that, so odd counts lose the larger half.
I compared the stack total after rebalance with 38, counting any tiers that sit over budget after a promotion.
